title: Naturally shed feline-vibrissa + shrimp-chitin reinforced bacterial-cellulose biotube formed in a confined tubular geometry

user_reported_precursor_observation.report: In a previous experiment, nutrient SCOBY culture was formed in a long narrow dropper-like tube and produced a cellulose-like filament/matrix extending through the tubular geometry rather than a conventional flat pellicle.
user_reported_precursor_observation.user_interpretation_at_time: culture of fungus growing in both directions
user_reported_precursor_observation.registry_interpretation: PRESERVE_AS_USER_REPORTED_OBSERVATION; bacterial cellulose in SCOBY systems is commonly produced by acetic-acid bacteria such as Komagataeibacter, while yeasts coexist in the consortium. The observed object must be independently identified before assigning fungal or bacterial origin.
required_confirmation: cellulose identity by FTIR/Raman or equivalent
microbial identity if organism attribution matters
photographic/provenance record of the original run

external_feasibility_anchor.finding: Published work demonstrates biosynthesis of bacterial-cellulose tubes in cylindrical oxygen-permeable molds, and a 2026 study reports filament-like BC biocomposites formed inside gas-permeable silicone tubing.
external_feasibility_anchor.implication: The confined tubular geometry is a literature-supported BC-forming architecture; it does not by itself validate the proposed feline-vibrissa/chitin reinforcement.

sources.title: Production of bacterial cellulose tubes for biomedical applications
Artificial Symbiosis for Bulk Production of Bacterial Cellulose Composites
sources.note: Abstract reports filament-like biocomposites formed within gas-permeable silicone tubing.

material_architecture.intended_structure: BC matrix grown in situ around longitudinal or twisted vibrissa reinforcement while dispersed chitin becomes physically incorporated in the matrix
mechanical_concept: axial load sharing by long high-aspect-ratio keratin fibers
crack bridging and controlled pull-out by intact vibrissae
chitin phase as secondary reinforcement/interface modifier
tubular geometry as a shape-directing mold
not_assumed: chemical bonding of intact whisker cuticle to BC
strength superiority over BC-only or chitin-only controls

accepted: naturally shed intact vibrissa with provenance
probable naturally shed intact vibrissa with no sign of cutting or plucking
rejected: trimmed or cut vibrissa acquired for the experiment
forced removal from a live cat
sample with attached living follicular tissue unless independently shown to have shed naturally

process.action: Collect and label only naturally shed vibrissae; preserve source/provenance and initial as-found state.
Use traceable shrimp-derived chitin with preparation history and characterize identity, residual protein/mineral fraction and particle-size distribution before attribution of any effect to chitin.
Prepare two candidate architectures: longitudinal intact vibrissae and a gently twisted/plaited bundle of naturally shed vibrissae. Do not damage the fibers merely to force braiding.
Place the vibrissa architecture inside a narrow cylindrical mold/tube designed to preserve oxygen access; introduce the characterized chitin phase without assuming it will remain uniformly suspended.

Fill the mold with a standardized nutrient BC-producing SCOBY-derived culture and allow bacterial-cellulose formation around the reinforcements. Exact medium, loading, geometry, duration and environmental parameters must be preregistered for each run rather than inferred from this conceptual record.
Recover the formed biotube/filament, record wet geometry and mass, apply the project-approved cleaning/inactivation/conditioning workflow, and preserve both wet-state and conditioned-state specimens.

Verify matrix continuity, fiber incorporation, chitin distribution and interface before mechanical claims. Test axial tension, bending, crush/compression, pull-out, wet retention and—if a hollow lumen is retained—leak/burst behavior under a dedicated safe materials-testing setup.

G0_IDENTITY: chitin identity and residual protein/mineral fraction
G3_MECHANICAL: optional leak and burst metrics for hollow specimens
G4_REPRODUCIBILITY: matched filler volume fraction where cross-material comparison is made

reverse_chain: HIGH_STRENGTH_BIOTUBE requires measured gain over matched controls
measured gain requires continuous BC wall/filament plus effective load transfer
effective load transfer requires vibrissae to be embedded rather than freely sliding
combined benefit requires chitin to be retained/distributed rather than sedimented or washed away
continuous BC formation in a tube requires sufficient viable BC producer, nutrients and oxygen access
oxygen access depends on tube material/geometry and cannot be assumed from a liquid-filled capillary
material attribution requires confirmation that the produced filament is cellulose and not merely fungal/yeast biomass
ethical admissibility requires naturally shed vibrissae only

critical_breakpoints.failure_mode: BC production localizes only where oxygen is available, causing discontinuous tube/filament
smooth keratin cuticle yields poor adhesion and excessive fiber pull-out
particles agglomerate/sediment or alter culture behavior rather than reinforcing
apparent bidirectional growth is biomass or surface film rather than a continuous BC tube
vibrissa and chitin each work alone but interfere when combined

literature_support_for_modern_material_l.claim: Keratin and cellulose can form mechanically useful composites and hydrogen-bonded interactions.
literature_support_for_modern_material_l.boundary: Used dissolved human-hair keratin and plant cellulose; not intact feline vibrissae or bacterial cellulose.

literature_support_for_modern_material_l.claim: BC/chitin nanofiber hybridization can improve mechanical/barrier properties in composite films.
literature_support_for_modern_material_l.boundary: Nanofiber film system; not shrimp-particle-loaded tubular growth around intact whiskers.

literature_support_for_modern_material_l.claim: BC tubes can be biosynthesized in cylindrical oxygen-permeable molds.
literature_support_for_modern_material_l.source: International Journal of Biological Macromolecules 2021, DOI 10.1016/j.ijbiomac.2021.08.011

claim_ceiling: Do not call the product 'especially strong' until matched mechanical data support that claim.
Do not infer that the prior tube experiment proves fungal growth or BC identity without characterization.
Do not infer that ancient Egyptians made SCOBY, chitin-cellulose, or whisker-reinforced biotubes.
Do not equate cat hair in ancient recipes with feline vibrissae specifically unless a text or physical sample distinguishes them.
Do not use plucked or deliberately cut vibrissae in this research line.
